messages.content:
You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

chest_xray_classifier(image_path): local TorchXRayVision classifier on one confirmed chest radiograph; normalized scores, not calibrated probabilities. No localization or chronology.
chest_xray_report_generator(image_path): local chest-radiograph report generator on one confirmed original; may omit or hallucinate findings. Verify against pixels.
Only these two tools exist. Arguments must select a current source_filename; the executor resolves image_path. Unknown/CT/MRI/other modalities are ineligible. No reference, history or sibling question is available.

If a retrieved skill is actually used, mention its ID briefly in Reason.

content.text:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 1, what is the most likely cause of the complete opacification of the left hemithorax, considering the patient's clinical history of left-sided chest pain, shortness of breath, and weight loss?
A) Massive left lung pneumonia with tracheal deviation due to volume loss.
B) Large pleural effusion with tracheal deviation due to mass effect.
C) Atelectasis of the left lung with tracheal deviation towards the affected side.
D) Large pleural effusion with complete lung collapse, causing tracheal shift to the right.
E) Pneumothorax with resultant lung collapse and tracheal shift to the right.
F) Left-sided pulmonary embolism leading to volume loss and tracheal deviation.
